why: The marshal's muster faces south and the route brings the party to him from the north; his watch turns only to a warder, and the party member who answers him may be a wanderer, so he is judged by his own yaw and the party walks up to his back (162 degrees off his facing). It declares no unit: a body may watch one class, and what the engine refuses is a talked-to body whose watch cannot be relied on to turn it, facing away from the approach. Taking the marshal's watch away no longer refuses: an NPC with no `watch` watches the nearest player by default.
